24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. ... 24.2 Vendor may not assign this Agreement, delegate material performance, or transfer it by change of control without Customer's prior written consent, not to be unreasonably withheld ... 24.4 Customer's change of control does not give Vendor a right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service.</quote>
<parameter name="rationale">Section 24 sits at (indeed substantially at) our preferred position. Customer may assign without Vendor consent both to an Affiliate (as defined in § 1.1) and to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets (24.1); Vendor may not assign, delegate material performance, or transfer by change of control without Customer's prior written consent, subject only to a reasonableness standard (24.2); other assignments are mutually consent-gated on a not-unreasonably-withheld basis (24.3); and Customer's change of control expressly gives Vendor no right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service (24.4). Section 13 (p0056) is consistent, permitting Customer to transfer licence rights to an Affiliate or successor in connection with a Section 24 assignment, and no termination provision contains a change-of-control trigger. The only shortfall against preferred wording is that the competitor bar reads "may never assign to a direct Customer competitor without Customer's consent" rather than an absolute prohibition; because 24.2 already blocks any Vendor assignment absent our consent, this is a minor sub-element noted for information only and not redlined.
